name: Aqua
lede: Aqua, as a color name on screens, means pure full-strength cyan, #00FFFF; it is the web name for a color that older sources call a light greenish blue.

sections.title: Water, and a web color
sections.body:
The word comes from the Latin for water, and as a color name it means water-like: Paterson defines it as a light greenish blue, a name that web designers adopted with the hex code #00FFFF [1]. The same dictionary lists *aqua* among the 16 basic VGA colors and the 140 names of the X11 set used for web pages [1][2]. On screens aqua is identical to cyan: our library shows a distance of zero between the two, and other near-duplicates such as bright cyan and bright turquoise sit within two units [3].

That makes aqua unusual among named colors. It is not an object or a flower, it is the full-strength blue-green that a screen can produce, with the red light switched off and green and blue at full [3]. It is a screen color, and real paint is unlikely to match it.

sections.title: Other aquas in the books
sections.body:
Paterson also records a street use. The color aqua was one of the many colors in which the lamp-posts of Notting Hill were painted for the 1999 Carnival [1]. The dictionary lists aqua blue and aqua green as separate entries [1], and our library holds [[aqua-blue]] and [[aqua-green]] as their own colors, Maerz and Paul recording aqua green in 1927 [3].

Finlay describes a living example. The cotton breeder Sally Fox found, among naturally brown cotton plants, a boll of raw cotton in an unexpected aqua green, which she described as sea turquoise mixed with moss and mint in a foam of white [4]. Brown cotton was already a surprise, and the green and the pale pink she later found were unplanned finds of crossing, not a dye [4].

Most of the other times *aqua* appears in the books we hold, it is the first half of *aqua regia*, *aqua fortis* or *aqua vitae*, the acids and spirits of the alchemists, and has nothing to do with color [5]. Drebbel's tin-scarlet story, which involves aqua regia, is a disputed tale and not a color origin for aqua [5].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body:
No painting in our archive of 23,781 has a color within CIEDE2000 distance 4 of aqua covering even 1 per cent of its canvas, as photographed [6]. That describes the archive, not painting as a whole, and it makes sense: #00FFFF is a screen-only extreme [6].

The closest things to aqua in the world are not paints but [[turquoise]] and the paler [[light-cyan]] and [[pale-turquoise]], each of which a painter can reach [3].

origin.first_recorded: as a web color name, X11 and HTML; no earlier color use recorded in our sources

choices: A mix of purple and white

openers: On a screen, aqua and cyan are the very same color: red off, green and blue at full strength.
